name: LEAPS Short Put
summary: Sell a put with more than a year to expiry for a large upfront credit. Obscure and capital-inefficient: theta per day is minimal and the collateral is locked up for years.
breakevens: strike - credit, often 25-40% below spot, which is the one genuine appeal

greeks.theta: positive but tiny per day - less than 0.1% of the credit daily, which is the core problem
greeks.vega: strongly negative - the dominant greek. A vol spike produces a large mark-to-market loss long before any delta loss

when_to_use: Almost never for an income system. Theta is the slowest of any short-premium structure per unit of collateral. Selling 30-45 DTE puts repeatedly earns several times more per year on the same capital.
entry_rules: Cash >= strike x 100 x contracts, locked for potentially two years
IVR > 50 required - nothing less justifies the capital lock-up
Maximum 1 such position; notional <= 10% of equity
Default: DISABLED. The 30-45 DTE CSP dominates it on every metric except breakeven distance
management_rules: Close at 50% of credit - which on a LEAPS put often takes 12+ months
Consider closing at 40% of credit if reached within 6 months; the remaining theta is not worth the remaining time
Roll only into a shorter-dated position, never longer
exit_rules: Close at 50% of credit (or 40% if reached early), at the 2x stop, or when DTE < 120 - at which point convert to a standard 30-45 DTE CSP cycle
All never-assign triggers from cash-secured-put apply: extrinsic < $0.10, delta > -0.85, 14:30 ET expiry-day proximity check, 15:45 ET backstop
assignment_risk: LOW while far OTM and far from expiry, rising sharply if it ever goes deep ITM - at which point the collapsed extrinsic makes early assignment likely and you are delivered shares at a strike set two years earlier.
buying_power: Full strike x 100 in cash, locked for the duration. This opportunity cost is the strategy's real cost.
liquidity_needs: LEAPS put markets are wide; require spread <= 6% of mid and OI >= 100.
common_mistakes: Being seduced by the large absolute credit while ignoring credit-per-day-per-dollar-of-collateral; ignoring the vega mark-to-market swings in the interim.
